title: policy-eval-underflow-replay-race-causing-negative-credit-reads-and-fallback-misrouting
creator: Sasha Patel
description:
Summary: We observed customer reports of unexpected token debits and transient negative credit readings for per-org and per-key quotas following a leader failover and shard replay. This causes the policy evaluator to believe a key is overdrawn and triggers fallback routing to lower-tier models and emergency throttles, impacting a subset of high-throughput customers.

Why this matters: Incorrect negative balances both expose customers to throttles when they have capacity and cause billing/accounting mismatches that require manual reconciliation. The behavior also increases latency as fallback paths are activated.

Scope: Affects multi-tenant rate engine when a shard undergoes leader failover while in the middle of a batched debit window. We have ~12 incidents in the last month, recurring on the same autoscale boundary and at similar traffic patterns.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a shard pair and create synthetic load that generates continuous per-key debits + intermittent metadata updates (route aliases).
2) Force leader failover (kill leader process) during a 250ms batching window (observed window of vulnerability).
3) Observe the follower apply a replayed set of deltas while a concurrent flush applies a local delta, causing the in-memory accumulator to reapply and move below zero.
4) Trigger policy eval: policy-evaluator treats negative reading as insufficient credit and routes to fallback and emits OverdrawnEvent to billing pipeline.
investigation_notes: Initial signal: customers opened support tickets with stack traces and trace-ids (trace: 8b7a3f...).
Reproduced in staging with deterministic harness built by infra; failure correlates with leader election occurring inside the batching window and quick reconnection of old leader.
Heap/accumulator inspection: applyDelta sequence shows duplicate applies when replay logs are reprocessed without idempotency guard.
RPC and protobufs: deltas do not include a monotonic apply-sequence id for batched sub-operations (only for snapshots), resulting in ambiguous dedup semantics on follower apply path.
Related observations: fallback routing was too eager — policy-evaluator used the instantaneous (race-affected) reading instead of a persisted confirmed-credit snapshot.
root_cause: A race between batched local debit flush and asynchronous replay application on follower after leader failover. There is no per-delta idempotency token for sub-batch operations, and the in-memory accumulator can be moved negative by re-applying the same debit. Policy evaluator reads instantaneous in-memory value and treats negative as under-credit, triggering fallback routing and throttle events.
mitigation_plan: 1) Hotfix (P0) - On policy-evaluator read path, clamp negative accumulator reads to zero and treat negative as eventual-consistency window: delay fallback decisions for keys with recent leader failovers (temporary guard). This reduces customer impact immediately.
2) Disable eager fallback for affected orgs via org-level feature flag for 24-72h until fix ships.
3) Communication: Post incident status to SRE/Support and notify affected customers with rollback/reconciliation steps.
long_term_fix: 1) Add immutable per-sub-batch apply-sequence IDs to deltas so followers can deduplicate replays deterministically.
2) Make apply path idempotent for sub-batch operations and update accumulator to be monotonic with transactional compare-and-set semantics under leader-change events.

3) Change policy-evaluator to consider 'confirmed' persisted snapshot timestamps and to use read-after-confirmation semantics for quota-critical decisions; fallback can use degraded heuristics only after confirmation timeout.
4) Add chaos test that injects leader failovers during batching windows and assert no negative accumulators or false fallbacks occur.

notes_from_reviews: Engineering review (2026-01-18) - callout from runtime team to avoid quick hotfix that masks root cause; prefer short-lived guard and follow-up with proper idempotency change.
PM feedback (2026-01-20) - prioritize customer communication; include reconciliation script to correct any billing overdraws.
Design/UX (2026-01-22) - recommend adding a console flag that surfaces recent leader failures per-organ to help triage customer queries.

next_steps: Ship hotfix branch that clamps negatives and gates fallback for keys with leader-change < 10s (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/1489) — owner: Maya.
Run chaos test suite nightly against staging and block merges until green for 3 consecutive runs — owner: Infra team.
Begin implementation of idempotency tokens and transactional apply path (split across two sprints) — owners: Runtime & Storage teams.
Prepare customer comms + billing reconciliation script and coordinate with Support & Finance — owner: PM (Jordan Ruiz).
